item.description:

It was never the greatest task management app, but if you liked Microsoft To Do you now need to wave it goodbye.

item.title: Apple supplier TSMC cuts off China chip orders amid tighter export controls
item.description:
TSMC, a key Apple supplier and the company that makes its A- and M-series iPhone and Mac chips, has suspended some advanced chip orders for Chinese companies following the tightening of United States semiconductor export restrictions.


TSMC has had to suspend orders from Chinese companies. Image credit: TSMC

Under the revised rules, TSMC can no longer provide Chinese companies with chips built using the 16nm or smaller manufacturing process. That is, unless a U.S. export license has been granted or they qualify for an exemption.

This new restriction means that Chinese companies are limited to chips that use much older technology built on the 28nm or 40nm processes. As a result, they will not be able to make use of the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) employed by AI data centers.

item.title: How to keep watching DVDs with VLC as Apple phases out Mac DVD support
item.description:
Apple has started retiring the technology behind its built-in DVD playback starting in macOS 27. Here's how you can still watch discs on a Mac with an optical drive and VLC.

VLC on Mac

For now, the change affects developers, not people watching DVDs on their Macs. Apple has removed the DVDPlayback framework from the macOS 27 SDK, so developers can no longer build apps against it with that SDK.

The framework itself remains in macOS 27, and Apple says it won't be removed until a future release. DVD Player also remains available and functional in macOS 27.

If you have movies on DVD, you don't have to wait for another macOS update to find a different way to play them. The free VLC app can open a DVD as a disc, giving you access to its movie, menus, chapters, audio tracks, and subtitles.

item.title: UK can't hide that it tried ordering Apple to allow access to user data
item.description:
A tribunal has ruled in favor of Apple and against UK government's attempt to keep secret it ordering backdoor access to encrypted iPhone data.


UK Parliament - image credit: Parliament

Apple is the firm that refused to create a way for the FBI to gain access to users' encrypted iPhone data, so it was never likely to do it for a foreign country. Nonetheless, the UK first tried back in 2016, and then in 2024 changed its own laws to allow it to make such demands secretly.

The UK then ordered Apple to create such a backdoor and used that law to forbid the company from revealing the order. The government issued what it calls a Technical Capability Notice (TCN), which, if Apple had complied, would give it access to any or all users' encrypted data worldwide.

item.title: Nvidia's board is clear that they don't want Jensen Huang back
item.description:
Trump, Elon Musk, and Jensen Huang himself have pushed to ignore Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy, but Nvidia's board of directors isn't having it.


Jensen Huang (left) will not be reinstated as Nvidia CEO. Colette Kress (right) is now interim CEO of the firm - images credit: Nvidia.

Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO after it was revealed that his multiple affairs included one with a suspected Chinese spy, and before the board could fire him. But backed by Trump and Silicon Valley bosses, Huang said on November 17, 2026, that he would return as CEO if Nvidia would only ask him.

In the Nvidia earnings call later that same day, however, the company's board of directors and new interim CEO said no. Chairman Harvey Jones said that the company would not be taking questions about the issue, but that he did want to open with some remarks.
